All three work. We've got tags **and** notes now living on the shared edit screen. The note is just a free text box, so the real choice is **how you add tags**. Open the three below; each has your bookmarks, and the NASA one has no tags yet.

In **each**, do the same: press **Edit** on the **NASA** bookmark, add the tags **space** and **science**, type a short **note** (e.g. *"Cool telescope facts"*), and **Save**. Watch how adding tags feels.

- **Option A — type a tag, press Enter:** http://maker:4001/tags-a.html
  Each tag becomes a little removable chip.

- **Option B — same chips, plus your existing tags to reuse:** http://maker:4001/tags-b.html
  Same typing, but it also shows tags you've used before (like *recipes*, *reference*) — click one to reuse it instead of retyping. This helps keep tags consistent as the collection grows. Try clicking an existing tag too.

- **Option C — one comma-separated line:** http://maker:4001/tags-c.html
  Type all tags in a single box, separated by commas.

Two things I decided that I'd like you to check: on each bookmark, tags show as **#chips** and your note shows as a **highlighted line** beneath the description. Tell me if that's how you'd want them to appear.

**After trying them, tell me which tag-entry style fits you best — and whether showing tags as chips and the note as a highlighted line works for you.**
